original_question: Are mutations in the SERPINA1 gene that result in deficiencies in functional alpha-1 antitrypsin considered genetic risk factors for emphysema?

final_qi.question: Are mutations in the SERPINA1 gene that result in deficiencies in functional alpha-1 antitrypsin considered genetic risk factors for emphysema?
final_qi.long_answer: SERPINA1 encodes the serine-protease inhibitor alpha-1 antitrypsin (AAT). Pathogenic variants such as the Z (E342K) and S (E264V) alleles reduce the circulating level and/or functional activity of AAT. When AAT is deficient, neutrophil elastase and other proteases are insufficiently inhibited in the lung, accelerating destruction of alveolar walls and producing panacinar emphysema, typically at an earlier age and with less smoking exposure than sporadic chronic obstructive pulmonary disease. Numerous epidemiologic, clinical, and mechanistic studies, as well as guidelines from organizations such as the World Health Organization, American Thoracic Society, and European Respiratory Society, recognize AAT-deficiency variants in SERPINA1 as established genetic risk factors for emphysema and COPD. Therefore mutations in SERPINA1 that impair functional alpha-1 antitrypsin are indeed considered genetic risk factors for emphysema.
